source_spans.locator: Nature Neuroscience 8(12), published p.1704 / PDF p.1, abstract and introduction: two action-choice systems trade computational simplicity against flexible/statistically efficient use of experience; relative prediction uncertainty is proposed as the basis for deploying the more accurate estimate

Nature Neuroscience 8(12), published p.1705 / PDF p.2, controller contrast and Figure 1: one pathway stores scalar long-run state-action summaries, whereas the other explicitly represents possible successor states/outcomes and computes values by branching search

Nature Neuroscience 8(12), published pp.1706-1707 / PDF pp.3-4, arbitration and uncertainty sections: for a given action the more certain value estimate is used; the two valuation methods have distinct uncertainty sources and profiles, including search noise versus data-inefficient bootstrapping

Nature Neuroscience 8(12), published pp.1709-1710 / PDF pp.6-7, Methods: both pathways evaluate actions in the same state/action task, one estimates posterior task transition/reward structure and derives value distributions by search, the other stores posterior state-action value distributions; lower posterior variance selects the winning value estimate before stochastic action choice

Nature Neuroscience 8(12), published p.1708 / PDF p.5, Discussion: both pathways can pursue identical rational ends despite different computational implementations; strict separation is a simplifying approximation and partial integration is acknowledged

institutions: Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, University College London
Interdisciplinary Center for Neural Computation, Hebrew University

conditions: an episodic action-choice problem is represented by states, available actions, transition contingencies and outcome utilities, with the exact task structure initially unknown and potentially changing over time

two approximate valuation pathways evaluate the same state-action choice: one stores value distributions learned from experienced transitions, while the other estimates transition/outcome structure and searches it at choice time
the source's formal comparison assumes the two pathways are strictly separated for analysis, while acknowledging that biological implementations may interact
prediction uncertainty is treated as ignorance about the true long-run value rather than as inherent stochasticity of reward delivery
substrate: two proposed computational action-choice systems conventionally associated with prefrontal and dorsolateral-striatal circuitry
task: estimate the long-run value of available actions and choose an action when two valuation pathways may differ in accuracy
temporal_scope: stored distributions and estimated task structure are updated across experience; structured search recomputes distal consequences from the current task estimate, and value comparison occurs for the current state-action choice

relations.description: experienced transitions update stored state-action value distributions through bootstrapping from stored successor values
experience is used to estimate posterior transition and outcome structure for the structured-search pathway
search over estimated successor states and outcomes maps the current state-action pair to a distribution over long-run value
the stored pathway's prediction uncertainty is quantified by the posterior variance of its value distribution
the search pathway's prediction uncertainty is quantified by the posterior variance of its value distribution
for each state-action pair, the winning estimate is the mean supplied by the pathway with the smaller posterior variance
winning values for the actions available in the current state determine stochastic action-selection probabilities

the two pathways address the same state-action valuation problem but differ in internal representation and computational route: one stores long-run value distributions directly, whereas the other represents transition/outcome structure and derives values by search
